result:
The proposed answer of 1 is not supported by the argument given, so I reject it.

The c < 1 case is correct: width below treewidth is impossible by definition. The argument for c = 1 is weak. It asserts that any width-n decomposition of the n×n grid forces spread Ω(log n) at some bounded-degree vertex, but the "balanced branching" step is only sketched and does not establish this bound. The step showing P(c) holds for every c > 1 is the bigger gap. The grid construction is only described loosely, and the general-graph case rests on an unproven "balanced separator-based construction" with an unjustified constant c' = O(1/ε). Nothing shows that the spread bound survives for arbitrary graphs at width (1+ε)·tw. The problem asks for a threshold, so the answer depends on a real constant-factor lower bound and matching construction. The proposed solution establishes neither, and the true threshold is plausibly larger than 1.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 2
